messages:
Maya CSM: quick draft — tiny runbook for go-live handoffs. goal: reduce renewal risk by standardizing a light prefilling + streaming strategy that customer teams can follow. keeping it 6 steps max.
Sam SRE: love it. can you add a quick cmd snippet for checking warm pools? that helps eng when we triage.
Maya CSM: yes. adding a small checklist and one-liner checks. also adding a short telemetry note for renewal signals.
Liam Eng: couple notes from runtime: prefer 'hydration window' of 90s for small tenants, 5m for medium. batching strategy: prefer adaptive batching with max_batch_size=16 and latency_slo=250ms.
Maya CSM: putting that in step 2. also propose fallback policy to non-streaming if early token errors > 0.5% for >5m.
Sam SRE: sounds good. include this one-liner for warm pool probe:
```bash
# probe GPU warm pool count for tenant xyz
redwoodctl pools list --tenant=xyz --status=warm --short
```
Maya CSM: added. step-by-step snapshot: 1) preflight signals, 2) warmchain hydration, 3) adaptive batch defaults, 4) streaming sanity check, 5) renewal escalation trigger, 6) feedback capture.
Liam Eng: define the signals in 1): active-requests-1m, median-latency-1m, early-token-errors-1m, prefill-hit-rate. risk score formula:
`risk = min(1, (0.6 * low_prefill_hit) + (0.3 * high_early_errors) + (0.1 * rising_latency))`
Maya CSM: adding concrete thresholds: low_prefill_hit = prefill_hit_rate < 0.4, high_early_errors = early-token-errors-1m > 0.005, rising_latency = median-latency-1m > 400ms.
Sam SRE: add runbook actions for the escalation: immediate throttled-prefill, open a case with the customer, enable dedicated burst for 15min, and schedule an enablement call.
Maya CSM: wrote short script for capture of customer feedback at go-live:
```text
Please tell us: 1) Did initial responses match expectations? 2) Any repeated truncation or delays? 3) Anything we should prefill for next session?
```
Liam Eng: telemetry note: tag all go-live traffic with `x-cs-run:go-live-<tenant>` so we can slice traces and generate a quick health card for the first 24h. gives us a single view for renewals team.
Maya CSM: adding that header as mandatory for enablement-runbooks. also: small UX tip — suggest customers send a short warmup prompt (2-3 sample queries) rather than bulk prefill; it's cheaper and warms kv cache.
Sam SRE: agree. also fallback policy: if streaming dropouts > 1% for >10m then switch to batched non-streaming with longer deadline and alert eng-sre.
Maya CSM: final ask: can eng produce a one-click checklist link (internal) that runs the warm-pool probe and tags telemetry? if yes i'll include link in the playbook.
Liam Eng: yep — i'll put a tiny run button in the internal console. will ping when done.
cs-bot: deploy-bot: preflight run completed for tenant sandbox-42 at 1770136800 :white_check_mark:
Maya CSM: perfect — once console button ready i'll run this with the customer during handoff. adding :thumbsup: and filing this as the "go-live light" runbook for small/medium tenants.
Sam SRE: copy. can we have a 1-paragraph TL;DR for CS handouts?
Maya CSM: drafted TL;DR — "Before go-live, run the warmchain probe, perform a short sample warmup, enable adaptive batching with defaults, monitor the 1m risk signals, and trigger the escalation steps if thresholds are breached. Capture immediate feedback via the three-question card."
Liam Eng: :thumbsup: small tweak: add suggestion to set quantization profile to 'latency-first' for chat flows.
Maya CSM: added. thanks all — i'll convert this to the formal doc and share a link here once it's in the playbook library.
